title: Aggregate jail decline can coexist with heavy and unequal pretrial exposure
source_unit: Bureau of Justice Statistics Census of Jails and Annual Survey of Jails estimates

denominator.unit: local jail custody and admission estimates from BJS Census of Jails and Annual Survey of Jails

unconvicted_share.unit: percent of persons held at midyear

observations.method: BJS 2024 Census of Jails and 2014-2018 and 2020-2023 Annual Survey of Jails; custody counts, admissions, rates, conviction status, and stay estimates are kept as separate administrative measures.
observations.uncertainty: Admissions are not unique people; midyear custody and annual flow use different denominators; estimates and state comparisons reflect reporting, facility coverage, definitions, and timing boundaries.
observations.subgroup: Local jail inmates and admissions; race and ethnicity, conviction status, sex, age, state, and jurisdiction comparisons are reported.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower population and admissions than 2014 indicate long-run contraction in some aggregate measures; high admissions and unconvicted share do not establish wrongful detention, cause of crime, or later harm.

related_sources.claim: BJS describes the Census of Jails coverage and the move to annual collection beginning in 2024.
BJS publishes the broader correctional-populations context for prisons, jails, probation, and parole.

boundary: This record measures local-jail custody, admissions, conviction status, stay, and unequal exposure. It does not follow unique people through court disposition, release conditions, housing, work, health, reentry, later justice contact, or trust.
